L01.gets: the first 3 jobs of a search are scored whatever the clock says

L02.gets: job titles in your own places are sorted past the clock

L03.gets: every stage counts from the press, so a press ends in 3 minutes

L04.gets: no AI call starts in the last seconds of the press

L05.gets: the job boards step ends at its share of the press

L06.gets: the best employer sites are always read, the rest are kept and read first next time

L07.gets: a press that scores first reads the jobs' facts with the seconds scoring leaves, from the same end

L08.gets: EURES is read from the first second of the press

L09.gets: the first press asks for its job boards once the employers are named, not in front of them

L10.gets: a press reads the job boards first; a first press reads its slice first and scores employer jobs without waiting for the boards

L11.gets: no AI round is forced per board, so scoring starts early

L12.gets: calls that failed do not shrink the next batch

L13.gets: jobs found earlier and never scored are scored from the run's first second, in one list with the new ones, the nearest first

L14.gets: among jobs in your places, the ones nearest your best place come first

L15.gets: EURES reads the regions near you first, the country last

L16.gets: one job waiting for a score does not hold back the titles of your places

L17.gets: the nearest batch of titles, from any reader, is asked next and its jobs are scored as it lands

L18.gets: EU portal jobs reach title sorting and scoring while there is time

L19.gets: waiting title batches move up once their places are learned

L20.gets: readers whose distance is unknown take turns, none takes every call

L21.gets: a slow place call holds only the jobs whose place it is asking; jobs in places already known go to your list at once (owner, 10 Nov 2026, asked via AskUserQuestion in session sa: "Only the asked jobs wait (Recommended)")

L22.gets: a city written with accents stays in the places a search reads

L23.gets: a round of title calls that fits before the stop is taken

L24.gets: a reader's titles are sorted in one pass, your places first

L25.gets: employers seen hiring in your places are read first

L26.gets: employers stay readable through an AI outage or a lost cache

L27.gets: a source whose AI step is refused fails alone, the press goes on

L28.gets: a press ended by time says Partial, never "Completed"

L29.gets: big job boards are read whole and their open jobs stay open

L30.gets: the job boards are asked for together, not one after another

L31.gets: the AI's judgment of a title wins over role and excluded words

L32.gets: a title gets a second look before a role-word hit leaves the list

L33.gets: the first press keeps scoring until a 70+ job, up to 10 (when no scorer runs beside the search; with one the slice scores 3 and that scorer goes on, L38)

L34.gets: a press after the first is one search: waiting jobs scored first, the job boards read inside it beside the employer sites

L35.gets: a repeat Find jobs run scores its waiting jobs beside the search: the employer sites are read while they are scored

L36.gets: a repeat Find jobs run starts the job boards first and reads the employer sites beside them, not after them

L37.gets: each Find jobs run saves what every step left for the next one, as counts the planner reads

L38.gets: a Find jobs run scores each job as it lands, beside the readers, to the run's end: no seconds are kept for the job facts and no job is paid for twice

L39.gets: jobs from the EU portal are placed on the map the moment they are read, so the jobs in your own area are sorted and scored first

L40.gets: the part of a Find jobs run that collects jobs never waits for a score: the one scorer beside it takes each job, ranked again at each new arrival
